title: Bread basics in the older shape
subtitle: Invented test content, written the way older packs were

lessons.title: Proving and baking
lessons.objective: Tell when a loaf is ready for the oven.

cards.prompt: Proving is the last rise, after shaping and before baking. A loaf that has proved enough holds a fingertip dent for a moment, then slowly fills it.

options.text: The first mix of flour and water
options.feedback: That is mixing, which comes first.
Cooling comes after; proving comes before the oven.

cards.feedback: Proving sets how open the crumb will be.

cards.prompt: The rise in the first minutes of baking is called oven ___.
cards.feedback: Oven spring ends when the crust sets.

cards.prompt: Match each tool to the loaf it holds.
Which of these show a loaf is ready to bake?

options.text: A fingertip dent fills back slowly
It has grown by about half
It has sunk at the top

cards.feedback: A slow-filling dent and a rise of about half: ready. Sunk means it went too far; firm means not far enough.

cards.prompt: Put these in order, from basket to oven.
cards.feedback: Out of the basket, scored, then straight into the oven.

cards.prompt: Which of these names mean the same thing?

options.note: Brushing the top with egg or milk.

cards.feedback: Scoring and slashing are the same cut.

cards.prompt:
The oven log reads:
"Deck 2 slow to heat, 40 min"
The first loaves are shaped and proving. What do you do?

options.text: Heat the oven now, and slow the proving in the cool room
options.feedback: The oven needs its forty minutes; the cool room buys them.

options.text: Bake the loaves in deck 2 straight away
options.feedback: A cold deck gives a pale, flat loaf.

options.text: Leave the loaves, and heat the oven once they are ready
options.feedback: By the time the oven is hot, the loaves are over-proved.
